statements.status_notes: Parsing a CMS AuthEnvelopedData or EnvelopedData message with maliciously crafted AEAD parameters can trigger a stack buffer overflow. A stack buffer overflow may lead to a crash, causing Denial of Service, or potentially remote code execution.
statements.impact_statement: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path links OpenSSL: the JRE uses its own Java TLS and crypto providers and none of its native libraries link libssl or libcrypto, lpm is a statically linked Go binary, and the only binaries in the image that link libssl (the wget, curl and openssl command-line tools) are never invoked after the image is built. The only binary in the image that references OpenSSL's CMS routines is the openssl command-line tool, so the vulnerable AuthEnvelopedData and EnvelopedData parser is never called by Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.21 (jammy; Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 shipped 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19 and 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.20) and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.7 (noble; Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 and 5.0.3 shipped 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.6); Liquibase Secure 5.1.0 and later ship 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.7 or newer.

statements.status_notes: Writing large, newline-free data into a BIO chain using the line-buffering filter where the next BIO performs short writes can trigger a heap-based out-of-bounds write. This out-of-bounds write can cause memory corruption which typically results in a crash, leading to Denial of Service for an application.
statements.impact_statement: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path links OpenSSL: the JRE uses its own Java TLS and crypto providers and none of its native libraries link libssl or libcrypto, lpm is a statically linked Go binary, and the only binaries in the image that link libssl (the wget, curl and openssl command-line tools) are never invoked after the image is built. No binary or library in the image other than libcrypto itself references BIO_f_linebuffer, and OpenSSL's own command-line tool only uses that filter on VMS, so the vulnerable line-buffering BIO is never used by Liquibase Secure. Fixed in Ubuntu libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.21 (jammy; Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 shipped 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19 and 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.20) and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.7 (noble; Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 and 5.0.3 shipped 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.6); Liquibase Secure 5.1.0 and later ship 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.7 or newer.

statements.impact_statement: This issue requires an application to verify attacker-supplied signed PKCS#7 data through OpenSSL's legacy PKCS#7 parsing APIs. Liquibase Secure's container runtime is a Java CLI launched by a shell entrypoint, and a source review found no OpenSSL PKCS#7 integration or invocation of OpenSSL tooling at runtime. The vulnerable OpenSSL code path is therefore not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: An uncommon OpenSSL DANE TLSA client configuration can trigger a use-after-free or double-free during server authentication when specific TLSA records are processed.
statements.impact_statement: This issue affects OpenSSL clients that perform DANE TLSA-based server authentication with a specific mix of PKIX and DANE-TA usages. Liquibase Secure's runtime is a Java CLI launched by a shell entrypoint, and a source review found no OpenSSL DANE/TLSA integration or other native OpenSSL client code paths. The vulnerable OpenSSL behavior is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL can dereference a NULL pointer while processing a malformed delta CRL during X.509 certificate verification when delta-CRL handling is enabled.
statements.impact_statement: This issue requires OpenSSL X.509 verification with delta-CRL processing enabled and a malformed CRL input. Liquibase Secure's runtime is a Java CLI launched by a shell entrypoint, and a source review found no native OpenSSL certificate-validation integration or CRL-processing path. The vulnerable OpenSSL code path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL can dereference a NULL pointer while processing crafted CMS EnvelopedData that uses KeyAgreeRecipientInfo, causing a denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: This issue affects applications that pass attacker-controlled CMS EnvelopedData into OpenSSL's CMS_decrypt() path. Liquibase Secure's runtime is a Java CLI launched by a shell entrypoint, and a source review found no OpenSSL CMS integration or invocation of native tooling that would process CMS EnvelopedData. The vulnerable OpenSSL code path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.impact_statement: This issue affects applications that pass attacker-controlled CMS EnvelopedData into OpenSSL's CMS_decrypt() path with RSA-OAEP transport parameters. Liquibase Secure's runtime is a Java CLI launched by a shell entrypoint, and a source review found no OpenSSL CMS integration or native RSA-OAEP processing through OpenSSL. statements.status_notes: On 32-bit platforms, OpenSSL can overflow a heap buffer while converting an excessively large OCTET STRING from an X.509 certificate extension into hexadecimal text.
statements.impact_statement: This issue affects only 32-bit platforms when OpenSSL converts excessively large X.509 OCTET STRING values to hexadecimal text. The scanner-reported package record is for amd64, and Liquibase Secure supports only 64-bit container architectures in this runtime. The required 32-bit execution environment is therefore absent.

statements.status_notes: Applications using OpenSSL RSASVE key encapsulation can disclose uninitialized buffer contents to a malicious peer if encapsulation is attempted with an invalid RSA public key.

Liquibase Secure's runtime is a Java CLI launched by a shell entrypoint, and a source review found no native OpenSSL key encapsulation integration or other OpenSSL API usage at runtime. The vulnerable code path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.impact_statement: This issue affects applications that pass attacker-supplied ASN.1 input into OpenSSL d2i_* decoders such as d2i_X509() or d2i_PKCS7(). Liquibase Secure's runtime is a Java CLI launched by a shell entrypoint, and a source review found no native OpenSSL ASN.1 decoding integration or invocation of OpenSSL tooling at runtime. statements.status_notes: Issue Summary: Cryptographic Message Services (CMS) processing fails to perform sufficient input validation on the cipher and tag length fields of AuthEnvelopedData containers, leading to various potential compromises. Attackers may achieve key-equivalent functionality for a given CMS recipient and/or bypass integrity validation for a given message.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE affects OpenSSL CMS AuthEnvelopedData decryption when attacker-supplied content reaches CMS_decrypt() and the application trusts the result without separate integrity enforcement. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL CMS tooling, and a source review found no references to CMS_decrypt, AuthEnvelopedData, or related CMS processing in the product runtime path. libssl3 is inherited from the base image only, so the vulnerable CMS path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: A certificate with many nameRelativeToCRLIssuer CRL distribution points causes disproportionate heap growth when OpenSSL caches X.509 extensions: a certificate chain under the accepted peer size limit can allocate several hundred MiB of resident memory during a normal TLS handshake, enough to crash a client or a server that solicits client certificates. OpenSSL rates the issue Low; no CVSS vector has been published.
statements.impact_statement: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path links OpenSSL: the JRE uses its own Java TLS and crypto providers and none of its native libraries link libssl or libcrypto, lpm is a statically linked Go binary, and the only binaries in the image that do link libssl or libcrypto (the wget, curl and openssl command-line tools, plus the coreutils digest utilities on noble) are never invoked after the image is built. OpenSSL never receives a peer certificate from Liquibase Secure, so its X.509 extension cache and CRL distribution point processing are never exercised. Fixed in Ubuntu libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.30 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.2); every published 5.x tag ships an older build.

statements.status_notes: When EVP_PKEY_derive_set_peer() is called with a DHX (X9.42) peer key, the peer key is not properly checked for subgroup membership. The realistic attack surface is narrow, principally CMP deployments with long-lived RA/CA DHX keys and bespoke applications using X9.42 static keys.

statements.status_notes: The implementations of AES-SIV and AES-GCM-SIV mishandle the authentication of Additional Authenticated Data with an empty ciphertext, allowing a forgery of such messages.

statements.status_notes:
Issue summary: A specially crafted PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed message could trigger a use-after-free during PKCS#7 signature verification.
Impact summary: A use-after-free may result in process crashes, heap corruption, or potentially remote code execution.
When processing a PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed message, if the SignedData digestAlgorithms field is present as an empty ASN.1 SET, OpenSSL may incorrectly free a caller-owned BIO during PKCS7_verify(). A subsequent use of the BIO by the calling application results in a use-after-free condition.
In the common case this occurs when the application later calls BIO_free() on the BIO originally passed to PKCS7_verify(). Depending on allocator behavior and application-specific BIO usage patterns, this may result in a crash or other memory corruption. In some application contexts this may potentially be exploitable for remote code execution.
Applications that process PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed messages using OpenSSL PKCS#7 APIs may be affected. Applications using the CMS APIs for this processing are not affected.
The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not affected by this issue, as the affected code is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.
statements.impact_statement: OpenSSL PKCS#7/S/MIME signature verification use-after-free. The scanner reported Ubuntu Jammy libssl3 packages below fixed package 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.25, but this assessment does not rely on a version-fixed claim because the OS package version is inherited from the base image rather than pinned in repository source. Liquibase Secure inherits OS packages from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2), and the runtime entrypoint dispatches to user-supplied commands or /liquibase/liquibase rather than OpenSSL PKCS#7 tooling (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8, docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:109, docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119, docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:121). The vulnerable path is not reachable: a focused grep for PKCS7_verify, PKCS7_, PKCS7, PKCS#7, S/MIME, SMIME, smime, BIO_free, and digestAlgorithms across repository sources returned zero hits.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL's generic elliptic-curve scalar multiplication, used for ECDSA and SM2 signing with curves that have no dedicated constant-time implementation (Brainpool and other generic prime curves), pads the secret scalar with non-constant-time BIGNUM operations. An attacker able to measure signing times can learn information about the per-signature nonce and, over many signatures, recover the private key. The NIST curves P-256, P-384 and P-521 are not affected.
statements.impact_statement: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path links OpenSSL: the JRE uses its own Java TLS and crypto providers and none of its native libraries link libssl or libcrypto, lpm is a statically linked Go binary, and the only binaries in the image that do link libssl or libcrypto (the wget, curl and openssl command-line tools, plus the coreutils digest utilities on noble) are never invoked after the image is built. Liquibase Secure never performs ECDSA or SM2 signing through OpenSSL; the JRE's Java providers handle any signing the product does. Fixed in Ubuntu libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.30 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.2); every published 5.x tag ships an older build.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL DTLS endpoints can retain disproportionately large amounts of memory when future-epoch records are buffered during a handshake, enabling denial of service through memory amplification.
statements.impact_statement: This issue affects OpenSSL DTLS endpoints that buffer future-epoch records during a handshake. Liquibase Secure's runtime is a Java CLI launched by a shell entrypoint, and a source review found no DTLS server or client implementation through OpenSSL, nor any invocation of OpenSSL networking tooling at runtime. The vulnerable DTLS code path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL CMS decryption sizes the key-unwrap output buffer based on querying the unwrapped key size, but the AES-WRAP-PAD unwrap primitive can write and cleanse more bytes than that query reports, causing an 8-byte out-of-bounds heap write.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29, but this issue is only reachable when an application decrypts attacker-supplied CMS messages through OpenSSL's CMS_decrypt path. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL CMS tooling, and a source review found no references to CMS_decrypt, AES-WRAP-PAD CMS unwrapping, or related OpenSSL CMS handling in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: The OpenSSL Certificate Management Protocol (CMP) caches additional certificates (extraCerts) sent in a CMP message, but never expunges them if the message is rejected. If a server reuses a single OSSL_CMP_CTX for the lifetime of a server process, a malicious client may flood it with requests and cause unbounded memory growth.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29, but this issue is only reachable when a long- lived CMP server reuses an OSSL_CMP_CTX across attacker-supplied requests and caches extraCerts from rejected messages. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than an OpenSSL CMP server, and a source review found no references to OSSL_CMP_CTX, extraCerts, or CMP request processing in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: When verifying the password-based MAC protection of a CMP message, OpenSSL reads the protectionAlg algorithm parameter with X509_ALGOR_get0() and treats the returned value as a PBMParameter after checking only that the pointer is not null, without validating the ASN.1 type. A remote attacker can crash an application acting as a CMP server that accepts PBM-protected messages, or a CMP client talking to a malicious or intercepted CMP server, causing a denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29, but this issue is only reachable when an application verifies CMP password-based protection on attacker-supplied messages. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL CMP tooling, and a source review found no references to CMP, PBM, or OSSL_CMP request-processing paths in the product runtime.

statements.status_notes: A signed integer overflow when sizing the destination buffer for Unicode output in ASN1_mbstring_ncopy can lead to a heap buffer overflow. The issue requires an application to call ASN1_mbstring_copy or ASN1_mbstring_ncopy directly, or to register a custom string type via ASN1_STRING_TABLE_add with attacker-controlled input large enough to overflow the size calculation.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.25, but this issue requires an application to call OpenSSL's ASN1_mbstring_copy or ASN1_mbstring_ncopy APIs directly, or to register a custom string type and then feed it extremely large attacker-controlled input. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL string-processing APIs, and a source review found no references to those OpenSSL ASN.1 entry points in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: For ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-OCB, EVP_Cipher could report successful decryption for an empty ciphertext without verifying the supplied AEAD tag. Applications that rely on EVP_Cipher to validate the tag in that case might accept forged messages.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29, but this issue requires an application to use OpenSSL's EVP_Cipher one-shot API for ChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-OCB decryption on an empty ciphertext while expecting that call to validate the AEAD tag. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL AEAD decryption helpers, and a source review found no references to EVP_Cipher, ChaCha20-Poly1305, or AES-OCB in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: A CMP client that identifies the certificate to revoke with a PKCS#10 CSR dereferences a NULL pointer and crashes when a malicious or compromised CMP server returns a crafted name in the revocation response. The response passes message-protection checks before the affected code runs, so the attacker must control the server or hold the protection secret.
statements.impact_statement: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path links OpenSSL: the JRE uses its own Java TLS and crypto providers and none of its native libraries link libssl or libcrypto, lpm is a statically linked Go binary, and the only binaries in the image that do link libssl or libcrypto (the wget, curl and openssl command-line tools, plus the coreutils digest utilities on noble) are never invoked after the image is built. Liquibase Secure contains no CMP client, so OpenSSL's revocation response handling is never reached. Fixed in Ubuntu libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.30 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.2); every published 5.x tag ships an older build.

statements.status_notes: An established DTLS 1.2 association using an AEAD cipher suite can be torn down by a single unauthenticated datagram whose encrypted fragment is shorter than the explicit IV and authentication tag overhead: the record layer passed the impossible length to the cipher before checking it and treated the rejection as a fatal internal error instead of discarding the record.
statements.impact_statement: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path links OpenSSL: the JRE uses its own Java TLS and crypto providers and none of its native libraries link libssl or libcrypto, lpm is a statically linked Go binary, and the only binaries in the image that do link libssl or libcrypto (the wget, curl and openssl command-line tools, plus the coreutils digest utilities on noble) are never invoked after the image is built. OpenSSL's DTLS record layer is never used by Liquibase Secure, so no DTLS association exists to be torn down. Fixed in Ubuntu libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.30 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.2); every published 5.x tag ships an older build.

statements.status_notes: SM2 signature generation in OpenSSL uses variable-time BIGNUM operations on the secret nonce and the private key, so signing time depends on secret values. An attacker able to measure SM2 signing times can learn information about the per-signature nonce and, over many signatures, recover the private key.
statements.impact_statement: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path links OpenSSL: the JRE uses its own Java TLS and crypto providers and none of its native libraries link libssl or libcrypto, lpm is a statically linked Go binary, and the only binaries in the image that do link libssl or libcrypto (the wget, curl and openssl command-line tools, plus the coreutils digest utilities on noble) are never invoked after the image is built. Liquibase Secure never performs SM2 signing through OpenSSL. Fixed in Ubuntu libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.30 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.2); every published 5.x tag ships an older build.

statements.status_notes: OpenSSL's DTLS retransmission logic mishandles a handshake message write that was suspended part-way through: the retransmitted message is read from a stale buffer offset and overwrites the state the suspended write needs to resume. A peer can receive heap memory as plaintext handshake data, or the read can reach unmapped memory and crash the process.
statements.impact_statement: No process in the Liquibase Secure runtime path links OpenSSL: the JRE uses its own Java TLS and crypto providers and none of its native libraries link libssl or libcrypto, lpm is a statically linked Go binary, and the only binaries in the image that do link libssl or libcrypto (the wget, curl and openssl command-line tools, plus the coreutils digest utilities on noble) are never invoked after the image is built. OpenSSL's DTLS implementation is therefore never used by Liquibase Secure, and no DTLS handshake can be in flight for the retransmission logic to act on. Fixed in Ubuntu libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.30 (jammy, shipped by Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1) and libssl3t64 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16 (noble, Liquibase Secure 5.0.2 through 5.2.2); every published 5.x tag ships an older build.

statements.status_notes: Issue summary: When CMS password-based decryption (RFC 3211 / PWRI key unwrap) processes attacker-supplied CMS data, an attacker-chosen stream-mode KEK cipher can trigger a heap out-of-bounds read in kek_unwrap_key(). Impact summary: A heap buffer over-read may trigger a crash which leads to Denial of Service for an application if the input buffer ends at a memory page boundary and the following page is unmapped. There is no information disclosure as the over-read bytes are not revealed to the attacker.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE affects OpenSSL CMS password-based decryption when attacker-supplied CMS data reaches CMS_decrypt() or CMS_decrypt_set1_password(). Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL CMS tooling, and a source review found no references to CMS_decrypt, CMS_decrypt_set1_password, PWRI key unwrapping, S/MIME, or PKCS#7 processing in the product runtime path. libssl3 is inherited from the base image only, so the vulnerable CMS decryption path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.
